prompt: aiohttp FormData add_field bytes value no filename fallback
answer:
In the stable aiohttp implementation, passing a `bytes`, `bytearray`, or `memoryview` value without `filename` causes `filename` to fall back to the field name:

```python
data = aiohttp.FormData()
data.add_field("file", content)
```

This emits a `DeprecationWarning` and behaves as though:

```python
data.add_field("file", content, filename="file")
```

It also makes the form multipart. The warning says that in v4, bytes will no longer automatically create a file field; use an explicit `filename` or pass a `BytesIO` object instead. If `content_transfer_encoding` is supplied, this filename fallback does not occur. (Stable source: `aiohttp/formdata.py`; stable client reference.)

The latest/master source shown in the results no longer performs this fallback: bytes make the form multipart, but no filename is added unless one is explicitly supplied.
